notes.subject: aw
notes.rationale: A letter of Artaxerxes addresses the treasurers beyond the river directly: 'an bɛ a fɔ aw ye'.

notes.subject: Elaha
notes.rationale: אלהא is the Aramaic form of God's name-word; rendered Elaha, keeping the Aramaic shape rather than the Hebrew Elohim.

notes.subject: wari-sara · dɔgɔkun-sara · sira-sara
notes.rationale: Three Persian loanwords for taxes (mindah tribute, belo excise, halak road-toll) rendered by their function: money-tax, goods-tax, road-tax.

notes.subject: כל
notes.rationale: The Aramaic kol governs the whole list of temple personnel; folded into 'o bɛɛ kan' at the end rather than repeated before the list.

translation: An bɛ a fɔ aw ye: sarakalasebaga minnu bɛ yen, Lewiw, kandibagaw, dabotigaw, Netinimw (tɔgɔ minnu bɛ Elohim so nin kɔnɔ baara kɛ), ani so nin dɛmɛbaga — o bɛɛ kan, fanga si tɛ sɔrɔ ka wari-sara walima dɔgɔkun-sara walima sira-sara da u kan.
